questions.question: Industrial production of Methanol (wood spirit) involves the catalytic reaction of water gas (CO + H₂) with hydrogen at 450°C and 200 atm over which catalyst?
questions.explanation: CO + 2 H₂ xrightarrow{ZnO + Cr₂O₃, 450°C, 200 atm} CH₃OH (methanol).

questions.question: In the fermentation of molasses or starchy grains to produce Ethanol, which two enzymes secreted by yeast convert sucrose into glucose/fructose and then ethanol?
questions.explanation: Invertase hydrolyzes sucrose into glucose and fructose: C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ + H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + C₆H₁₂O₆. Zymase ferments hexoses into ethanol: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2 C₂H₅OH + 2 CO₂.

questions.question: Rectified spirit obtained from industrial distillation of fermented wash contains approximately what percentage of alcohol by volume?
questions.explanation: Rectified spirit is an azeotropic mixture containing 95.6% ethanol and 4.4% water boiling at a constant 78.15°C.

questions.question: Methylated spirit (denatured alcohol) is rendered unfit for human drinking by adulterating ethanol with:
questions.explanation: Methanol (toxic), pyridine (foul-smelling), and coloring dye are added to industrial ethanol to prevent its misuse for recreational consumption without excise tax.

questions.question: In the Lucas Test for distinguishing primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols (reagent: anhydrous ZnCl₂ + concentrated HCl), a tertiary alcohol shows:

options.A: Immediate appearance of an oily turbidity/cloudiness (alkyl chloride layer)
options.C: No turbidity at room temperature unless heated

questions.explanation: Tertiary alcohols react immediately at room temperature via stable 3° carbocations to yield insoluble oily R-Cl.

questions.question: Oxidation of a primary alcohol with acidified potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇/H₂SO₄) yields an aldehyde, which on continued oxidation produces:

options.B: A carboxylic acid having the same number of carbon atoms

questions.explanation: R-CH₂OH → R-CHO → R-COOH. Primary alcohols oxidize sequentially to aldehydes and then carboxylic acids.

questions.question: Secondary alcohols oxidize with acidified dichromate to yield:

options.B: Ketones having the same number of carbon atoms

questions.explanation: R-CH(OH)-R' xrightarrow{[O]} R-CO-R' (ketone). Ketones resist further oxidation except under severe conditions.

questions.question: Why do tertiary alcohols resist oxidation by acidified dichromate under neutral or mild conditions?

options.A: The tertiary carbon lacks an α-hydrogen atom bonded to it

questions.explanation: Oxidation requires removal of an α-hydrogen attached to the carbinol carbon; tertiary alcohols [(R)₃C-OH] have no α-hydrogen.

questions.question: Phenol is distinctly more acidic than aliphatic alcohols because:

options.A: The phenoxide ion (C₆H₅O⁻) is resonance-stabilized by delocalization of the negative charge over the aromatic ring, whereas alkoxide ions have no resonance stabilization
options.B: Phenol has a higher molecular weight
options.C: Phenol is a solid at room temperature
options.D: The benzene ring pushes electrons into the oxygen atom

questions.explanation: The phenoxide anion has 5 resonance contributors delocalizing negative charge into ortho and para positions, stabilizing it and driving proton loss (pK_a ~10 vs 16 for ethanol).

questions.question: Which of the following substituted phenols is the most acidic compound, rivaling mineral acids in strength?
questions.explanation: Picric acid has three strongly electron-withdrawing -NO₂ groups at ortho and para positions, stabilizing the conjugate base immensely (pK_a = 0.38).

questions.question: When phenol is treated with neutral ferric chloride (FeCl₃) solution, it produces a characteristic coloration of which color?
questions.explanation: Phenol reacts with FeCl₃ to form a water-soluble coordination complex [Fe(OC₆H₅)₆]³⁻ imparting a diagnostic violet coloration.

questions.question: Treatment of phenol with bromine water (Br₂/H₂O) gives an immediate white precipitate of:
questions.explanation: In water, phenol ionizes to strongly activating phenoxide ion, causing rapid tri-substitution at all activated ortho and para positions to yield insoluble 2,4,6-tribromophenol.

questions.question: In the Kolbe-Schmitt reaction, sodium phenoxide is heated with carbon dioxide at 125°C under 4-7 atm pressure followed by acidification to produce:
questions.explanation: C₆H₅ONa + CO₂ xrightarrow{125°C, 5 atm} Sodium salicylate xrightarrow{H⁺} Salicylic acid (precursor for Aspirin synthesis).

questions.question: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, phenol is heated with chloroform (CHCl₃) in aqueous NaOH at 60°C to introduce an aldehyde group ortho to -OH, producing:
questions.explanation: The electrophile dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂) attacks phenoxide to produce salicylaldehyde upon alkaline hydrolysis and acidification.

questions.question: Williamson Ether Synthesis involves an S_N2 displacement between:

options.A: A sodium alkoxide (R-O⁻Na⁺) and an unhindered primary alkyl halide (R'-X)
options.B: Two alcohol molecules with conc. H₂SO₄

questions.explanation: R-ONa + R'X → R-O-R' + NaX. Primary alkyl halides give high ether yields via backside S_N2 attack; tertiary halides undergo E2 elimination instead.

questions.question: What happens when an ether (R-O-R') is heated with an excess of concentrated hydroiodic acid (HI)?

options.A: It cleaves completely to form alkyl iodides and water: R-O-R + 2 HI → 2 R-I + H₂O

questions.explanation: Excess hot HI cleaves ethers: first to alcohol + alkyl iodide, then the alcohol reacts with second mole of HI to form another alkyl iodide.

questions.question: On prolonged storage in the presence of atmospheric oxygen and light, diethyl ether forms shock-sensitive explosive:
questions.explanation: Auto-oxidation creates dangerous peroxides: CH₃-CH(OOH)-O-CH₂CH₃; ether bottles must never be distilled to dryness if peroxides are present.

questions.question: Which reagent is used to detect dangerous peroxides in old samples of diethyl ether?

options.A: Aqueous KI and starch solution (yielding a blue color) or acidified FeSO₄ + KCNS (red color)

questions.explanation: Peroxides oxidize I⁻ to free I₂ (blue starch complex) and Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺ (deep red thiocyanate complex).

questions.question: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid), widely used as an analgesic, antipyretic, and blood thinner, is synthesized by the acetylation of salicylic acid with:

options.A: Acetic anhydride or acetyl chloride in the presence of an acid catalyst

questions.explanation: Salicylic acid + (CH₃CO)₂O xrightarrow{H⁺} Acetylsalicylic acid (Aspirin) + CH₃COOH.

questions.question: Bakelite, the historic dark thermosetting plastic, is manufactured industrially by the step-growth condensation polymerization of:
questions.explanation: Phenol reacts with HCHO under acidic or basic catalysis to form ortho- and para-hydroxybenzyl alcohols that cross-link into 3D network Bakelite.

questions.question: What is the common chemical name of 1,2,3-propanetriol, a trihydric alcohol with sweet taste and high viscosity?
questions.explanation: Glycerol is CH₂OH-CHOH-CH₂OH, having 3 hydroxyl groups engaged in extensive hydrogen bonding, giving it high boiling point (290°C) and viscosity.

questions.question: Which test chemically distinguishes Ethanol from Methanol?

options.A: Iodoform test (Ethanol gives yellow CHI₃ precipitate with I₂/NaOH; Methanol does not)

questions.explanation: Ethanol contains the CH₃-CH(OH)- grouping that oxidizes to CH₃CHO and gives positive yellow iodoform; methanol lacks this group.

questions.question: Why does ethanol have a much higher boiling point (78.3°C) than dimethyl ether (-24°C) despite having identical molecular formula (C₂H₆O)?

options.A: Ethanol molecules form intermolecular hydrogen bonds via the -OH group, while ethers cannot form intermolecular H-bonds with themselves
options.B: Ethanol has a higher molecular weight

questions.explanation: Intermolecular hydrogen bonding in liquid ethanol creates associated molecular clusters requiring significant thermal energy to vaporize.

questions.question: Dow's process for the industrial preparation of phenol involves heating chlorobenzene with 6-8% aqueous NaOH at 350°C and 300 atm pressure. The intermediate formed before acidification is:
questions.explanation: Nucleophilic aromatic substitution under forced conditions yields sodium phenoxide, which upon acidification with HCl yields free phenol.

questions.question: In the Cumene process for the manufacturing of phenol, isopropylbenzene (cumene) is oxidized with air to cumene hydroperoxide, which upon acid cleavage yields phenol and which valuable co-product?
questions.explanation: C₆H₅CH(CH₃)₂ + O₂ → Cumene hydroperoxide xrightarrow{H₂SO₄} Phenol + Acetone (in equimolar amounts).

questions.question: The Victor Meyer test is a diagnostic colorimetric method to differentiate 1°, 2°, and 3° alcohols. The colors produced by the resulting nitrolic acid/pseudonitrol in alkaline solution are:

options.A: 1° gives Blood Red, 2° gives Blue, 3° gives Colorless

questions.explanation: 1° alcohol forms nitrolic acid (red in alkali); 2° forms pseudonitrol (blue); 3° alcohol has no α-hydrogen and remains colorless.

questions.question: When diethyl ether is treated with concentrated sulfuric acid in the cold, it dissolves by forming a stable, water-soluble:
questions.explanation: Ether oxygen has basic lone pairs that accept a proton from concentrated strong acids to form protonated oxonium salts.

questions.question: Crown ethers (such as 18-crown-6) are cyclic polyethers remarkable for their ability to:

options.A: Selectively chelate and dissolve alkali metal cations (like K⁺) in non-polar organic solvents as phase-transfer catalysts

questions.explanation: The central hydrophilic cavity of 18-crown-6 matches the ionic radius of K⁺ (1.38 Å), dragging ionic salts (like KMnO₄) into benzene ('purple benzene').

questions.question: Catalytic dehydrogenation of ethanol vapor over heated copper catalyst at 300°C produces:
questions.explanation: CH₃CH₂OH xrightarrow{Cu, 300°C} CH₃CHO + H₂↑. Dehydrogenation converts 1° alcohols into aldehydes without risking over-oxidation.

questions.question: Catalytic dehydration of ethanol over Al₂O₃ at 350°C yields ethene, but at lower temperature (140°C with excess ethanol) it yields:
questions.explanation: At 140°C with excess ethanol: 2 C₂H₅OH xrightarrow{H₂SO₄ or Al₂O₃} C₂H₅-O-C₂H₅ + H₂O (intermolecular bimolecular dehydration).

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is also known as 'Carbolic Acid'?
questions.explanation: Phenol was historically named carbolic acid when first extracted from coal tar by Runge in 1834.

questions.question: Phenol reacts with phthalic anhydride in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄ to produce which popular acid-base indicator?
questions.explanation: Condensation of two moles of phenol with one mole of phthalic anhydride eliminates water to form phenolphthalein (colorless in acid, pink in base).

questions.question: What is the order of boiling points among isomeric primary, secondary, and tertiary butyl alcohols?
questions.explanation: Branching decreases molecular surface area and weakens van der Waals forces, while also sterically hindering hydrogen bonding; hence 1° > 2° > 3°.

questions.question: Ethylene glycol (ethane-1,2-diol) is widely used in automobile radiators as:

options.A: An antifreeze that depresses the freezing point of cooling water

questions.explanation: Ethylene glycol forms strong hydrogen bonds with water, depressing the freezing point down to -40°C while simultaneously raising the boiling point.

questions.question: Ethers are generally unreactive and chemically inert toward bases, oxidizing agents, and reducing agents because:

options.A: They lack an active, ionizable hydrogen atom and have stable C-O-C sigma bonds with no easily accessible polar π-systems

questions.explanation: The ether C-O bond is relatively strong and unreactive toward nucleophiles and bases in the absence of strong protonating acids.
